checks.do: Whether the remaining quota covers the hashes to be loaded, read from the tenant before a bulk load.

endpoint.statement: Sandbox keeps a custom list of MD5 file hashes it blocks, under /zia/api/v1/behavioralAnalysisAdvancedSettings: GET reads the list and PUT replaces it.

quotes: Returns the custom list of MD5 file hashes that are blocked by Sandbox.

two-shapes.statement: The list has two wire shapes. A flat `fileHashesToBeBlocked` array of strings, and a richer `md5HashValueList` of objects with `url` (the MD5), `urlComment` and `type`. The Python SDK documents `type` as CUSTOM_FILEHASH_DENY or CUSTOM_FILEHASH_ALLOW; the Go source illustrates it only as "MALWARE".

quotes: ``type`` (str): The type of hash, e.g., ``CUSTOM_FILEHASH_DENY`` or ``CUSTOM_FILEHASH_ALLOW``.

allow-entries.statement: Because the Python type includes CUSTOM_FILEHASH_ALLOW, the same list may hold allow entries as well as deny entries, so "blocklist" can understate what is in it.
allow-entries.conditions: Derived from the Python docstring and example, which pass an ALLOW entry in the same list; no source describes how Sandbox treats it.

clear-with-empty-array.statement: To clear the list, send `md5HashValueList` as an empty array. The Go payload field deliberately has no `omitempty` because the API requires the key even as `[]`; dropping the key does not clear the list.

quotes: Do not use omitempty - API requires md5HashValueList to be present (even as []) when clearing the list
Pass an empty list to clear the blocklist.

hash-count.statement: A sub-endpoint, /behavioralAnalysisAdvancedSettings/fileHashCount, returns `blockedFileHashesCount` and `remainingFileHashes`, the used and unused quota for blocking MD5 hashes. `remainingFileHashes` is how many more can be added.

quotes: Retrieves the Cloud Sandbox used and unused quota for blocking MD5 file hashes.

mcp-check.statement: The MCP workflow checks a suspect file by reading the blocked-hash list and looking for its MD5, and reads the hash count to see overall usage.

quotes: Returns the list of MD5 hashes currently blocked by Sandbox. Check if the file's hash appears in this list.
Returns blocked-hash usage statistics to understand overall sandbox activity volume.

sdk-functions.statement: In the Go SDK the list is `Get` (flat), `Getv2` (rich), `Update` (flat), `Updatev2` (rich) and `GetFileHashCount`. In the Python SDK `get_behavioral_analysis` reads it, `add_hash_to_custom_list` writes the rich shape, and `get_file_hash_count` reads the count.

tf-both-resources-registered.statement: The provider registers both `zia_sandbox_behavioral_analysis` and `zia_sandbox_behavioral_analysis_v2` as resources and data sources.

tf-v1-v2-same-endpoint.statement: The Terraform resources `zia_sandbox_behavioral_analysis` (flat) and `zia_sandbox_behavioral_analysis_v2` (rich) both read and write the same object: the SDK's `Get` and `Getv2` read, and `Update` and `Updatev2` PUT, the single behavioralAnalysisAdvancedSettings endpoint, differing only in payload shape.

tf-v2-encouraged.statement: The v2 resource documentation says the original `zia_sandbox_behavioral_analysis` resource is still available, but the provider encourages users to move to the new format, and that the original will eventually be deprecated.

quotes: is still available in the provider; however, we encourage users to move to this new format

quota-cap.title: The tenant's MD5 blocklist cap and whether it varies by subscription
quota-cap.detail: The SDKs return how many hashes remain but encode no absolute ceiling or tier dependence. The number is observable per tenant at runtime.

enum-and-help-framing.title: How Zscaler's help names this list and whether the type values are the documented set
enum-and-help-framing.detail: No help capture for this surface is vendored. Whether CUSTOM_FILEHASH_DENY and CUSTOM_FILEHASH_ALLOW are the complete documented values, or only what the Python SDK happens to use, is unknown.

tf-v2-supersedes-v1.title: Whether `zia_sandbox_behavioral_analysis_v2` is already required for new configurations
tf-v2-supersedes-v1.blocks: saying that new configurations must use the v2 resource rather than only should
tf-v2-supersedes-v1.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the legacy catalog said v2 supersedes the original resource. The provider docs only encourage the move and say the original will eventually be deprecated; both resources are registered and neither carries a deprecation notice in the provider registration. Whether v2 is already required for new configurations is not stated.

tf-v1-v2-coexistence.title: Whether declaring both Terraform sandbox resources in one configuration conflicts
tf-v1-v2-coexistence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: whether the v1 and v2 resources are separate backend objects is not confirmed in the provider docs, and because both use one endpoint and one fixed resource ID, declaring both in the same configuration may cause state conflicts. The sources show the shared endpoint and ID but not how two declarations of the same list would interact at apply or on refresh.
tf-v1-v2-coexistence.blocks: saying whether the flat and rich Terraform resources can be declared together
